app.name: Sem
app.tagline: Split group expenses fairly — at your own exchange rate.

hero.sub: Split group expenses in one sentence, at the table — converted at the rate you actually paid, not the one on the news.

problem.p1: Collect the receipts. Remember who ate what. Dig the exchange rate out of a card statement. Open the calculator on the last night of the trip — the least pleasant thirty minutes of the whole vacation.

title.before: One sentence in. A closed entry

method.sub: Nothing is deferred. Say what happened where it happened, and the amount is fixed with that moment’s rate and that table’s people.

chat.title: Type it like a text
chat.body: “Ramen 11875 yen, I paid.” That’s the whole interface — amount, currency and payer are read from the sentence.

items.title: Split by line item
items.body: Receipts break into items, and items attach to the people who had them. Whoever skipped the drinks doesn’t pay for the drinks.

checkpoint.title: Close the books mid-trip
checkpoint.body: Don’t wait for the last night. Settle to a checkpoint anywhere, and everything before it is frozen at its rate.

demo.title: Try a split.
demo.sub: Tap names and rates — the figures below follow the exact rules of the settlement engine. Your language sets the home currency: English defaults to USD, Korean to KRW.
demo.evenNote: Divides evenly — everyone pays the same.

remNote.before: The leftover goes to the payer — Alex pays

rates.p1: A travel card is loaded at different prices on different days. The same ¥11,875 costs each payer a different real amount.

p2.after: — what the money actually cost them. The market rate stays visible for reference, never as the basis.

rates.note: A $2.85 difference on one bowl of ramen — 71¢ per person, four ways.

principle.p1: When an amount doesn’t divide evenly, the remainder always lands in the payer’s favor. No banker’s rounding, no averaging it away.
principle.p2: The person who fronted the money should never lose by it. That’s a matter of trust before it’s a matter of arithmetic.

guide.title: How to use Sem
guide.intro: You record an expense in a few taps. A few more things worth knowing before you start.

why.rateTitle: It settles at what your money cost you
why.rateBody: Record what you paid to exchange money — ₩450,000 for ¥50,000 — and everything spent from that wallet settles at that rate. Today's market rate is fetched automatically when you need one instead.
why.receiptBody: Photograph it and the items come back as lines you can correct, rather than a total you have to break down by hand.
why.itemsBody: An expense can be split by who actually had each line, down to the quantity. Anything nobody claims is shared out.

steps.groupTitle: Join a group, or start one
steps.groupBody: An invite link puts you straight into your friend's group. Starting your own takes a name, the currency you will settle in, and where you are going.
steps.walletTitle: Add a wallet, then top it up
steps.walletBody: Exchanged cash, a travel card, a prepaid card — each one is a wallet. Add one from Wallets & top-ups in the menu, and recording a top-up is what teaches the app your own exchange rate.
steps.entryBody: The form sits right on the home screen — amount, who paid, who was in, one step at a time, without leaving the page. You can photograph a receipt there too, and the items come across with their prices.
steps.assignBody: Tick the people on each line, quantity included. Anything nobody ticks is shared between everyone on that expense.
steps.settleBody: Status, from the menu, shows what you fronted, what your own share came to, and what you are owed or owe with each person. Tap a name for the full history between the two of you.

guide.again: You can open this guide again any time from Account.

wallet.title: Wallets
wallet.payAsYouGoNote: Converted by the bank at purchase time — today's market rate.
wallet.overdrawn: {amount} over — a top-up is probably missing
wallet.overdrawnHint: More was spent from this wallet than was ever loaded onto it — so either you topped it up and never logged it, or an expense only came out of here in part. Manage wallets works the top-up out from what is really on it; the other one is fixed on the expense.

wallet.countNothing: Matches the records — nothing to adjust.
wallet.countShortfall: {amount} less than the records explain — spending of your own that never got logged.
wallet.countSurplus: {amount} more than the records explain. Money only gets into this wallet one way, so you topped it up and never logged it. What did it cost?

wallet.adjustmentRemoveConfirm: Remove this adjustment? The balance goes back to what the records say.
wallet.label: Name
wallet.deleteConfirm: Delete {label}? Its top-ups go with it. Only possible while nothing has been paid from it.
wallet.deleteBlocked: Expenses were paid from this wallet, so it stays.
wallet.none: No wallets yet. Add one for the cash or the travel card you're carrying.
wallet.tripPrompt: Heading to {place}? Log the cash you exchanged or the travel card you loaded, and every expense will convert at what your money actually cost.

loading.status: Sem is adding up who owes whom…

explain.WALLET_AVG_COST: Converted at what the money in that wallet actually cost — the average of its logged top-ups.
explain.MARKET_SNAPSHOT: Converted at the market rate captured when the expense was entered.
explain.ACTUAL_CHARGED: Uses the amount the payer's bank actually billed.
explain.MARKET_FALLBACK: That wallet has no top-ups logged yet, so the market rate was used.
explain.OWN_EXCHANGE_RATE: Converted at the rate you told us you exchanged at — money you prepaid but keep no wallet for.
explain.SPLIT_FUNDING: Paid from more than one source. Each part was converted at its own rate, so no single rate covers the whole amount.
explain.FROZEN: Settled at a checkpoint. The amount was pinned when that period closed, so nothing entered since can move it.

form.refundHint: Refund — negative amount, money coming back.

form.unassignedNotice: Unassigned lines are split in proportion to what each person had.

form.assignOver: That is {assigned} units of {quantity} — more than this line has. Fix it before saving.

form.rateBasis: Market rate. Your bank or card will charge a little more.
form.rateUnavailableInline: No live rate for {currency} — enter it manually on the next step.
form.manualHint: This is the MARKET rate for the day — not your own wallet's rate.
form.rateUnusual: This rate looks unusual — the market rate is {unit} {currency} = {rate} {settlement}.
form.paidFromQuestion: Was this prepaid money, or paid on the spot?
form.prepaidOptionNote: Cash or a travel card you topped up before spending it.
form.onTheSpotOptionNote: A card, or cash you changed at a booth and spent straight away. Converts at the market rate.
form.whichWallet: Which one did it come out of?
form.noWalletsYet: You have no wallets set up. Just tell us the rate you got — we can save it as a wallet afterwards if you want.
form.ownRateHint: The rate YOU exchanged at — not today’s market rate.

form.answerTill: I topped it up on the spot

form.answerOnTheSpot: I paid the rest on the spot

form.tillDialogNote: This is saved as a top-up of that wallet, dated to the expense.
form.answerSomeoneElseNote: They fronted part of this receipt, so the group owes them for it.
form.splitAdd: Some of it came from somewhere else
form.splitOver: That is {amount} more than the expense.
form.tillAmountLabel: How much you put on it ({currency})
form.reviewSplitTitle: Paid from more than one source
form.paidFromHint: Prepaid money converts at what that wallet cost you. A pay-as-you-go card converts at the market rate.
form.newCashWalletNote: We will start a cash wallet for {currency} when you save.
form.topUpQuestion: Exchanged more, or loaded your card?
form.addWalletLink: Add a travel card or another wallet
form.otherCurrencyWallet: You have {count, plural, one {a {currency} wallet} other {# {currency} wallets}}: {wallets}.
form.noteMarketMode: This group settles at the market rate, whatever it was paid with.
form.splitAgreesRounded: Rows add up to {sum} — {diff} more than the {total} total, because each share rounds up so the payer is never left short.
form.derivationRounding: Rounded up to the next whole {settlement} so the payer is never left short.
form.derivationSame: Same currency as the group, so no conversion.
form.derivationSplit: Converted part by part, each at the rate of whichever source paid it — so no single rate covers the whole receipt.
